title: Boeing still working with NASA to schedule next Starliner flight
summary: Boeing is collaborating with NASA to finalize the schedule for the next CST-100 Starliner flight to the International Space Station. The mission will be a cargo flight for the commercial crew vehicle.

title: Chinese startup raises funds for space situational awareness constellation, joining commercial SSA rush
summary: A Beijing-based startup raised $14 million to develop a satellite constellation for tracking orbital objects, contributing to China's expanding commercial space situational awareness (SSA) sector.

title: Swift reboost mission encounters attitude control problems
summary: A spacecraft launched to boost the orbit of a NASA astrophysics satellite is experiencing attitude control issues that may threaten its mission. The problems could jeopardize the Swift reboost mission's objectives.

title: ESA opens call to repurpose Gateway communications module
summary: ESA is exploring the possibility of repurposing the Lunar Link communications module, originally built for NASA's paused Gateway space station, for alternative uses. The agency has issued a call for proposals to assess the feasibility of this initiative.

title: NASA selects successor to CAPSTONE lunar mission
summary: NASA has chosen Advanced Space to lead a follow-up mission to CAPSTONE, aiming to test rendezvous and proximity operations in cislunar space. The new mission will build on the original CAPSTONE's objectives.

title: Upper C-band auction offers another lift for GEO industry
summary: The FCC's upcoming upper C-band spectrum auction is expected to generate over $6 billion, benefiting GEO satellite operators and funding new geostationary spacecraft and transition costs.

title: Sphinx Defense wins $287 million contract for strategic satellite communications software
summary: Sphinx Defense has secured a $287 million contract to develop mission planning software for the U.S. Space Force's next-generation strategic communications satellites, known as ESS. This award highlights the growing demand for advanced satellite communication solutions in defense applications.

title: Orbes unveils Exo-ORB and agreement with Symphony Space
summary: Orbes unveiled Exo-ORB, a free-flying satellite, and announced an agreement with Symphony Space to gather imagery of an uncrewed Symphony Space station. The collaboration marks a significant step in commercial space imaging and station monitoring.

title: Intel debuts new chip for space computing
summary: Intel has introduced a new chip named Starfire designed for space computing, enabling onboard data processing and AI workloads. This development marks Intel's expansion into the space industry with specialized hardware.

title: SpaceNews Welcomes Max Aliprandi as Business Development Associate
summary: SpaceNews announced the hiring of Max Aliprandi as Business Development Associate to strengthen its sales and business development teams. This move supports the company's expansion efforts.

title: DJI Lito 1 drone review
summary: The DJI Lito 1 drone is praised for its entry-level features, including omnidirectional obstacle sensing and good image quality. It is highlighted as an impressive drone for beginners.

title: NASA fuels its next-gen Roman Space Telescope for August launch
summary: NASA has successfully fueled its next-generation Roman Space Telescope, with the launch scheduled for August 30. The mission remains on track for its planned deployment.

title: Our Milky Way galaxy appears to have flipped 90 degrees long ago. But why?
summary: The Milky Way galaxy may have flipped 90 degrees in its past due to a major, unknown event. A slowly rotating stellar halo provided clues to this dramatic shift in the galaxy's history.

title: SpaceX launches 24 Starlink satellites to orbit in wake of Starship test flight (video)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched 24 Starlink satellites into orbit using a Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base. This mission followed the recent Starship test flight.

title: ISS meets Venus in incredible daylight photo | Space photo of the day for July 28, 2026
summary: An astrophotographer captured a rare daylight image of the International Space Station passing by Venus. This stunning photo was featured as the Space Photo of the Day for July 28, 2026.

title: On this day in space! July 28, 1851: The 1st photo of a total solar eclipse was taken by a Prussian daguerreotypist
summary: The first-ever photo of a total solar eclipse was taken by Prussian daguerreotypist Johann Julius Friedrich Berkowski on July 28, 1851, revolutionizing solar astronomy.

title: BALLS on the moon: China set to launch Africa's 1st lunar science mission in 2029
summary: China is set to launch Africa's first lunar science mission in 2029, sending three spherical probes to the moon's south pole aboard its Chang'e 8 lander. This mission marks a significant step in international lunar exploration collaboration.

title: Betelgeuse, Betelgeuse! Astronomers capture clearest image yet of famous star's elusive companion
summary: Astronomers have captured the clearest image yet of Betelgeuse's elusive companion star. This discovery is considered a significant breakthrough in stellar observation.

title: 'Crazy idea' succeeds: Scientists monitor space junk with radio telescopes
summary: Scientists successfully monitored space junk using radio telescopes for the first time ever. This breakthrough offers a new method for tracking orbital debris.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: Ship 40 successfully completed its mission and returned intact during SpaceX's Starship Flight 13, demonstrating its reliability and paving the way for future missions.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled worldwide this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket in China and a Falcon 9 rocket. The launches highlight ongoing activity in the global space industry.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft has discovered surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io during two recent flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the moon's volcanic activity and geological features.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to conduct hot-fire tests for the second stage of the New Glenn rocket on the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn rocket for its upcoming missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones during its third attempt. This marks another successful test for SpaceX's Starship program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully docked with the International Space Station (ISS), expanding the station's crew. A U.S. extravehicular activity (EVA) completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay highlights ongoing challenges in the Starship program's development.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman from Florida. This mission represents a significant step in robotic satellite servicing technology.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9, Starship, and Chinese rockets scheduled to launch
summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new attempt at launching Starship Flight 13 after last week's abort. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are scheduled for upcoming launches.

title: Making Progress: Relativity’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and PLD Space’s Miura 5
summary: Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space are making progress on their respective rocket developments: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5. While Starship's test program has garnered attention, these companies continue advancing their launch vehicle projects.

title: TEC Business to Business website
summary: TEC Business to Business website is mentioned in the context of space industry news, but no specific details or events are provided.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary by releasing a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over the past five decades. The publication underscores the agency's milestones in space exploration and technology.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together space startups and industry leaders to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technology for next-generation antennas, highlighting innovations in the space industry. It emphasizes the role of silicon as a critical component in steering these advanced antennas.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed electromagnetic compatibility tests in ESTEC's Maxwell Test Chamber, ensuring its electronics are space-ready. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting events to present the follow-up to the Council Meeting at Ministerial Level 2025 (CM25), detailing planned activities and industrial opportunities across its programs.

title: One robotic arm to rule them all
summary: A new advanced robotic arm has been developed for space applications, aiming to enhance satellite servicing and maintenance. This innovation could significantly reduce costs and extend the lifespan of orbital assets.

title: We’re back: Proba-3 ready for more science
summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and its main scientific instrument, ASPIICS, are fully operational and ready to resume formation flying to create artificial eclipses for scientific observations.

title: Space Science’s Golden Age Problem
summary: The White House OSTP released a comprehensive vision for the nation's research and development (R&D) enterprise. The initiative aims to address challenges in space science amid its perceived golden age.

title: Amazon Joins the Direct-to-Device Race
summary: Amazon has entered the direct-to-device satellite market by filing with the FCC to launch 5,105 low-Earth orbit satellites. This move positions Amazon to compete in the growing D2D space industry.

title: New Report Maps Potential Futures for Africa’s Space Ecosystem
summary: A new report explores potential future developments for Africa's space industry as the continent aims to establish itself as a significant space power. The report highlights strategic opportunities and challenges in the region's growing space ecosystem.

title: Rocket Lab Expands to Alaska with $266M Launch Contract
summary: Rocket Lab is establishing a new launch site at the Pacific Spaceport Complex-Alaska in Kodiak, with launches expected to begin by the end of this year. The expansion is supported by a $266 million launch contract.

title: ORBES Unveils Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft
summary: ORBES introduced the Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft, a 12U, sub-26-kg spacecraft designed for inspection missions and ready-to-go deployment on customer infrastructure. The spacecraft aims to support in-space maintenance and servicing operations.

title: Starship Sticks the Water Landing on Flight 13
summary: SpaceX successfully completed the 13th test flight of its Starship rocket, achieving the first intact water landing. The mission marks a significant milestone in the rocket's development.

title: ESA Puts €65M Behind Europe’s First Lunar Ice Rover
summary: ESA has committed €65 million to support Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. The funding marks a significant step toward lunar exploration and resource utilization.

title: Lunar Outpost Plans to Fly NVIDIA Chips to the Moon
summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA chips to the Moon, merging the semiconductor and lunar exploration industries. This move highlights the growing intersection of technology and space missions.

title: A Deep Dive into the Bluetooth Satellite Connectivity Market Following the FCC’s Proposal
summary: The FCC is proposing to open unlicensed Bluetooth and Wi-Fi frequencies for space-based communications. This move could significantly impact the Bluetooth satellite connectivity market.

title: FCC Filings Show Eutelsat is Working on a New 528-sat Constellation Beyond OneWeb
summary: Eutelsat is developing a new constellation of 528 satellites beyond its OneWeb program, though the 'Next' initiative is not yet fully developed. The company's plans were revealed in FCC filings.

title: Rocket Lab Nabs Largest Launch Award; Establishing Site In Alaska
summary: Rocket Lab secured a $266 million contract from the U.S. Space Force, marking its largest launch contract to date, which includes at least 12 suborbital launches. The company is also establishing a new launch site in Alaska.

title: Eutelsat Details IRIS² MoU With Poland
summary: Eutelsat has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Poland to support Europe's IRIS² satellite program. The collaboration will focus on developing secure satellite communications.

title: Impulse Space Details its First Electric Propulsion System
summary: Impulse Space has unveiled its first electric propulsion system, named Electra, designed for long-duration space operations. This follows the company's exploration of developing such a system a year ago.

title: Skywave to Add Iridium SBS Data Service Into Industrial IoT Offering
summary: Skywave and Iridium have formed a strategic partnership to integrate Iridium's Short Burst Data (SBD) services into Skywave's industrial IoT offerings for heavy equipment OEM customers. This collaboration marks the first integration of Iridium's SBD services into Skywave's platform.

title: Virgin Media O2 Exec Explains Strategic Approach to Direct-to-Device With O2 Satellite
summary: Virgin Media O2 has launched O2 Satellite, a direct-to-device service in the UK, leveraging its strong position in the mobile market. An executive explained the company's strategic approach to this new satellite-enabled offering.

title: Space-Based Data Centers: Inside the Race to Move Compute to Orbit
summary: The space industry is exploring the concept of space-based data centers to meet the growing demand for computing power driven by AI. Companies are racing to move some data center infrastructure into orbit to leverage the unique advantages of space.

title: SES Space & Defense Wins Space Station Connectivity Deal With Starlab
summary: SES Space & Defense has partnered with Starlab to develop a communication architecture for continuous space station connectivity. This collaboration aims to enhance connectivity solutions for future space stations.

title: Amazon Leo Files for 5,105 Satellites in Globalstar Spectrum for D2D
summary: Amazon has filed with the FCC to launch a Direct-to-Device satellite constellation of up to 5,105 satellites using spectrum from a Globalstar deal. This move aims to expand Amazon's satellite-based connectivity services.

title: SES Set to Receive $5.6B in Incentive Payments for C-Band Clearing
summary: SES is set to receive $5.6 billion in incentive payments for clearing the C-band, as announced by the FCC. Eutelsat will receive $504 million as part of the same program.

title: Via Satellite Rising Stars of 2026
summary: Via Satellite announces the third class of 25 Rising Stars for 2026, highlighting young professionals shaping the future of the space and satellite industry.
